- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and news volume drops, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply lagged correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile; if sentiment swings >0.50 in 3–5 days, forecast should be adjusted toward historical mean of last 10–15 days.
- When sentiment change is negative and news volume remains high, model often underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for delayed sentiment impact.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., >10% gap), reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 7–14 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
